title.narrative: Water Museums for the Virtual UNESCO Science Museum platform

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is leveraging the contribution of the Global Water Museums Network (WAMU-NET), a Flagship Initiative of the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP), to the establishment of the UNESCO Virtual Museum/ Centre platform on science and technology museums/centres, exhibiting a unique repository of the different forms of humanity’s connection with water, including its technical, scientific, natural and cultural heritage. WAMU-NET groups 89 museums and information centres on water in 38 countries (status of December 2023), and supports the creation and maintenance of museal and water information spaces worldwide. Several of the WAMU-NET member institutions already established virtual museum spaces, others are planning and developing them, with the network’s help. WAMU-NET’s contribution to the UNESCO Virtual Museum/ Centre, a unique multilingual and multidisciplinary Platform for knowledge sharing and promoting global cooperation will consist of the connection of existing virtual water museum/centres with the Platform; the development of virtual spaces based on existing exhibitions; and the collaboration and advice in developing and maintaining the Platform, jointly with UNESCO networks, including UNESCO Category 2 Centres, UNESCO Chairs, and UNESCO designated sites making it UNESCO-specific and distinct. The virtual museum will enhance STEM education and science popularisation and outreach by providing access to valuable educational resources, local contextualization, interactive exhibits, multimedia content, and archival materials for researchers, policymakers, students and the public. This Platform will advance open access to scientific information and promote more inclusive, transparent and equitable science for all, including women and girls.
